title: Replace tautological verifyNever(mockFacade...) checks on a facade never injected into the repo under test in epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart
why: Both 'no push when syncEngine is null (local-born user)' tests construct localRepo without a syncEngine: argument (defaults to null), so localRepo never holds a reference to mockFacade. Mocktail records invocations per mock instance, so verifyNever(() => mockFacade....) is checking an object the code under test never touches -- it passes unconditionally no matter what localRepo actually does internally. A regression that made a local-born repository push to Firestore through any other path would not be caught by this acceptance test despite its name promising exactly that guarantee, and the production code's current correct `_syncEngine?.push...` null-guard (verified in both TrackRepositoryImpl and LearningOrderRepositoryImpl) is protected by nothing but the fact the call would crash first.
recommendation: Delete the vacuous verifyNever calls (the preceding await already fails the test if a null syncEngine crashes on use), or replace with an assertion tied to localRepo's actual collaborators -- e.g. assert the local Drift write succeeded with no corresponding outbox/sync artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Neither 'no push when syncEngine is null' test references a mock object that isn't reachable from the object under test
A deliberately-introduced bug that makes the null-syncEngine path push anyway (e.g. via a stray ambient reference) fails one of these two tests
mergedFrom: Assert actual payload values, not just non-null, in epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart's 'push payload contains required fields' test
